flags.quote: Taking the knight on d4 with your c-pawn is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead.
flags.critique: I recaptured a knight with a pawn. That is not winning a bishop. If SEE of knight-minus-pawn lands in the 200cp bucket and you label that 'a bishop,' I will distrust every material sentence you utter. Tell me I recapture the knight and may get an isolated d-pawn — not that I am up a piece I did not win.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your f3-knight is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: This is the Open Sicilian recapture, not a tactic. Black just took on d4; I take back. Calling that 'undefended' and tagging wins_material teaches me that every recapture is a hanging-piece puzzle. Contrast ply 26, where Nxe4 really is a free pawn — same sentence, totally different chess.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on g6 with your f-pawn puts it at risk of attack from the black queen and pawn. A better move would have been taking the pawn on e6 with your f-pawn because you can likely skewer the black queen and the black e8-rook.
flags.critique: I dropped 356 centipawns and you shrugged 'puts it at risk.' The queen just recaptures on g6. fxe6 is not a skewer of queen and e8-rook — those pieces are not on one line. The real punch is the open f-file onto the queen on f6. Do not invent a skewer from a later PV event.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-rook to e8 is a blunder, but moving your d4-bishop to e5 would be better because you pin the pawn to the rook and then take another pawn.
flags.critique: I threw away a winning position (eval flips +536). 'Pin the pawn then take another pawn' is not a 500-centipawn idea. Bh6 was hitting my rook; running to e8 walks into the fxe6 crush. Be5 is the counterpunch that hits the queen on g3. Name the tactic I allowed, not a pawn-grab fairy tale.

flags.quote: Moving your e2-knight to g3 is a mistake, but moving your pawn to a4 would be better.
flags.critique: I put the knight on g3 where Ne4 takes it with check. That is the whole lesson. You never say the piece is hanging. 'Play a4 instead' with no because-clause is a move name, not coaching. If you cannot explain why Ng3 dies, do not pretend a4 is the teaching point.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on g3 with your queen is the strongest move because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: Again: recapture after Nxg3+. I am not winning material; I am taking back the piece that just took me. 'Undefended' plus wins_material is the same lie as Nxd4 on ply 7. I already know to recapture a checking knight.

flags.quote: A better move would have been moving your pawn to a4 because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: a4 hits the bishop on b3, not a pawn. 'Likely take a pawn' is a PV-follow-up guess wearing a capture costume. If the engine wants a4, tell me I harass the Sozin bishop — I am a 1200, I can understand 'attack the bishop.'

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The reason dump is backward_pawn and the sentence has no because. f4 kicks the knight on e5. That is beginner chess 101. You had kicked_by_pawn for when I get kicked; you stayed mute when I did the kicking. I learned nothing, and 'backward pawn' would have been a lie if it had surfaced.

flags.quote: Moving your h5-knight to f6 is the strongest move because it saves your f6-knight from capture.
flags.critique: The knight is on h5. It is not a f6-knight until after I move it. Nf4 was attacking h5; I retreat. Naming the piece by the destination square makes the sentence a joke: I saved the f6-knight by going to f6. Call it your knight, or your h5-knight.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e6 is the strongest move because you put more pressure on the center.
flags.critique: e6 kicks the knight on d5. I can see the knight sitting on d5. Do not lecture me about 'the center' while a piece is en prise to a pawn. This is the same empty center_control slot you used on c5, d6, and Nf6.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to f6 is a blunder, but taking the pawn on f5 with your e-pawn would be better because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: I blundered 231 centipawns. Taking a hanging pawn is ~100. You never say what Qf6 actually ruins — queen steps onto a square where Bg5 hits it, and I stop being winning. The played-move reason is 'pin,' which is not even in the sentence. Tell me the tactic I walked into.

flags.quote: Moving your c1-bishop to h6 leaves your pawn hanging to the black queen and pawn. A better move would have been moving your c1-bishop to g5.
flags.critique: Bg5 attacks the queen on f6. That is why it is better. You suggest Bg5 and then refuse to say it hits the queen. 'You left f5 hanging' is a pawn story for an 181-centipawn swing Lichess called a blunder. Also you stuffed ignored_threat in twice, which shows in the cadence even if I cannot see the dump.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d4 with your knight is the strongest move because you come out a pawn ahead.
flags.critique: I took a knight. Queen left d3 to recapture on g3, so d4 is hanging. If SEE then counts cxd4 Bxd4 and nets a pawn, say that: you take the hanging knight, and after the recapture you win the pawn. 'A pawn ahead' for Nxd4 makes me think the knight is worth a pawn.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your c-pawn is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the Open Sicilian trade — I swap a wing pawn for White's center pawn. No because-clause, and the hidden reasons are hanging, doubled_pawns, backward_pawn. None of those is the lesson. You treated a book recapture like a random capture.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on g3 with your e4-knight is the strongest move because you fork the white f1-rook and the white king and you take the defender of the white f1-rook.
flags.critique: I take a hanging knight with check. Yes the knight also eyes Rf1, but White recaptures with the queen and I do not win the rook. 'Fork the rook and king' plus 'take the defender of the rook' makes me expect a rook drop. The check and the free piece are enough.

flags.quote: Moving your c3-knight to d5 is playable, but moving your c1-bishop to g5 would be better because you pin the pawn to the queen.
flags.critique: Black's knight already left f6 for h5. Bg5 'pins' the e7 pawn to the queen — a pawn that was not going anywhere. That is not why Bg5 is better. Nd5 looks like the hole I am supposed to occupy; if you ding it, give me a real reason, not a detector firing on a useless relative pin.

flags.quote: Moving your king to h1 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Eval went +16 to −28 and you still said strongest, with zero reasons. Why did my king shuffle into the corner? Off the g-file? Off the long diagonal after …g6/Bg7? I am staring at a king move that looks like a mouse slip and you just said 'That's the one.'

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c5 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: This is the Sicilian. I am not 'controlling the center' like e4; I am fighting d4 and trading a c-pawn for a center pawn. Same sentence as e4, d6, Nf6. If every first-ten-moves lesson is center_control plus 'That's the one,' I will skip the coach.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on g6 with your queen is the strongest move because you fork the white h6-bishop and the white queen and you skewer the white queen, exposing the white pawn.
flags.critique: I recaptured the pawn and my queen attacks Bh6 and Qg3. Fine. Then you also call it a skewer that 'exposes the pawn.' Fork and skewer in one breath is tactic-salad. I recaptured and hit two pieces. Stop stacking geometry labels.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Empty reasons. g6 prepares Bg7 — Dragon/fianchetto, bishop coming to the long diagonal. That is the only thing I need to hear. 'Strongest move' with no because is a participation trophy.

flags.quote: Moving your f4-knight to e2 leaves your pawn hanging to the black f6-knight. A better move would have been moving your f1-rook to e1 because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: e4 was already hanging after …Nf6; Nf4 never defended e4 (knights do not guard adjacent squares). 'Leaves your pawn hanging' sounds like I created the leak. The real lesson is ignored_threat: defend e4 (Re1) or you lose it. Causal verb is wrong; the suggested fix is right.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Another empty strongest. h3 is prophylaxis: no Bg4 pin, no …Ng4. I play this in every Sicilian and still want to hear why, because otherwise it looks like a wasted tempo. You had nothing.

flags.quote: Moving your g8-knight to f6 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: Nf6 attacks e4. You proved you know that one ply later, when Nc3 'saves your pawn from capture.' So you can detect the threat and you still fed me center_control on the attacking move. Teach the attack on the pawn.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to d3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Empty again, 35cp dumped, still 'strongest.' …Nc6 just unveiled Bg7 onto Nd4. Qd3 defends the knight. That is a one-clause lesson you skipped so you could say That's the one.

flags.quote: Moving your f1-bishop to c4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Sozin/Fischer: the bishop aims at f7 and the king. 'Development' with no because is true and useless. You later notice the b3–f7 pin after Bb3; you could have introduced that diagonal here.

suggestions.title: Do not call recaptures winning material
suggestions.detail: Mark captures as recaptures when the captured unit just arrived on that square. Suppress wins_material and the 'undefended' / 'come out X ahead' because-clauses unless net material versus the start of the exchange is actually up. A 1200 hears ply 7 Nxd4 and ply 35 Qxg3 as tactics; they are take-backs. Keep that language for real hanging pieces like ply 26 Nxe4.

suggestions.title: Stop labeling knight-for-pawn as a bishop
suggestions.detail: materialLabel maps 200–249cp to 'a bishop', so pawn-takes-knight SEE (knight minus pawn ≈ 200) becomes 'a bishop ahead' on ply 37. Describe the exchange ('you win a knight for a pawn') or snap the label to the captured type when SEE is that capture minus a recapture, not the nearest piece-value bucket.

suggestions.title: Name saved pieces by origin, not destination
suggestions.detail: ownedPhrase uses the after-FEN square, so …Nf6 is 'saves your f6-knight from capture.' Pass the from-square (or drop the square) for saves_piece. A 1200 laughs; the chess was fine (Nh5 was hanging to Nf4).

suggestions.title: Treat kicking a piece as the lesson
suggestions.detail: kicked_by_pawn already exists as a problem when our piece gets hit. Mirror it as a benefit when our pawn move attacks an enemy piece (e6 vs Nd5, f4 vs Ne5). Gate center_control off those plies. This is the most common 'you talked about the center while I attacked a knight' failure in the game.

suggestions.title: Explain what the played move hung
suggestions.detail: On Ng3, Qf6, Re8, Bh6, fxg6 the coach names a better SAN and a weak because, and never states the tactic that made the played move bad (knight en prise with check; queen walks into Bg5; rook flees into fxe6; capturing on a square the queen recaptures). pickProblemReasons should win the first clause on mistake/blunder; suggestedBecause is second. A 1200 needs 'you hung X' before 'try Y.'

suggestions.title: Do not pin PV-later tactics on the first suggested move
suggestions.detail: verifyLikelyTactics already exists but still lets 'likely take a pawn' (a4 hits a bishop) and 'likely skewer queen and rook' (fxe6 opens the f-file onto the queen) through. Only attach capture/pin/fork/skewer to the suggested move if that tactic is created on ply 0 of the PV, and name the actual target type. 'Likely' is how you smuggle a later event into the first sentence.

suggestions.title: Prefer attacks and breaks over center_control in the opening
suggestions.detail: c5, d6, Nf3, d4, Nf6, Nc6, Bc4, g6 all collapsed to center_control or empty development. Add cheap opening facts: pawn-break (d4), recapture-of-break (cxd4), attacks-undefended-or-underdefended-pawn (Nf6 vs e4), bishop-aims-near-king (Bc4 vs f7), fianchetto-prep (g6) / long-diagonal develop (Bg7). You already detected 'Nc3 saves e4' — use the same attack on the Nf6 ply.

suggestions.title: Never say strongest with no because
suggestions.detail: g6, h3, Kh1, Nh5, f4, Qd3, c3, a5 are 'the strongest move' plus 'That's the one' and empty reasons. If rankReasons returns nothing, drop the strongest verdict (use 'a useful move' / skip) or require one concrete fact (prophylaxis vs Bg4, defends the hanging knight, prepares the fianchetto). Identical quips on every best move make the mascot feel like a slot machine.

whatWorked: Nc3: 'saves your pawn from capture' after Nf6 actually taught the e4 attack.
Castling copy is human: king tucks away, rook comes into the game.
Nf4: discovered attack from Bb3 onto e6 while the knight steps off d5 — real geometry.
Nc6: unveiling Bg7 onto Nd4 is the Dragon-bishop lesson I wanted on g6/Bg7.
Nxe4: 'the pawn was undefended' is the correct use of that sentence (unlike the recaptures).
Bb3: pin on the f7 pawn toward the king plus saving the bishop from Ne5.
